Defiant

/dih-FY-uhnt/ - the stress falls on FY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Defiant means boldly refusing to obey or to submit to authority.

Ordered ashore ahead of the storm, the tugboat captain answered with one defiant blast of the horn and made her run anyway.

Worked Example

The letter from the county was plain: the beloved treehouse violated setback rules and had thirty days to come down. Mr. Alvarez read it on his porch, folded it once, and nailed it to the treehouse ladder. He has since attended every hearing with a 1932 deed in hand, and the treehouse has entered its fourth summer, unmoved.

Defiant is the exact word because it names bold refusal to obey — resistance aimed up, at an authority that expects to be obeyed. Alvarez isn't merely stubborn about his own tastes; he is refusing an order, publicly, with the paperwork nailed where the county can see it. Take away the order and you'd have persistence; against the order, it is defiance.

How Defiant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

rebellious

rebellious: rises against the whole system; defiance can refuse a single order

insubordinate

insubordinate: the workplace and military version — disobeying a superior

Antonyms

obedient

obedient: does as told

submissive

submissive: yields without being told twice

How Strong Is It? — uncooperative → defiant → mutinous

uncooperative vs. defiant

uncooperative vs. defiant: Uncooperative drags its feet and misses deadlines; defiant looks authority in the eye and says no.

mutinous vs. defiant

mutinous vs. defiant: Mutinous goes past defiant — the refusal has become an organized rising to seize control.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of defiant.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away, un- (from Latin dis-)

Root — fi

Root — fi: to trust (Latin fidere)

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: inclined to

Put it together

Put it together: De- (away) + fi (to trust — Latin fidere) + -ant (inclined to) = trust withdrawn. Old French desfier meant to renounce your sworn faith — to tell your lord, out loud and in public, that you were his man no longer. Defiant still carries that scene: allegiance canceled to authority's face.

Use the root in a new word: confide

Use the root in a new word: confide: To confide in a friend is to place your trust with her — the same fid- root that defiance takes away.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / bold

Defiant is refusal with its chin up, and it needs someone with the standing to give orders — a court, a county, a commander. That need for an order separates it from this unit's contentious and pugnacious, which pick quarrels among equals. If no order has been given and someone simply won't budge, the honest word is stubborn, not defiant.
